title: Selective model-weight replacement
question: Can one selected model capability run from an AIR package with the original model unloaded while preserving held-out quality and reducing lifecycle-inclusive cost?
systems: AIR-only package with teacher and neural fallback unloaded
AIR-first hybrid with every model fallback logged
optional reference-fed AIR oracle ceiling, reported separately
requirements: same frozen task IDs and reviewed answers for all systems
pin llama.cpp server, GGUF model, quantization, revisions, hashes and flags
run AIR-only with no teacher model or neural fallback loaded
record every AIR answer and every hybrid fallback with reason and latency
report cold startup and warm inference separately
measure whole-host used memory and CPU-package energy with boundaries stated
report conversion time, energy, storage, lifecycle cost and break-even volume
reviewer assertions bind exact corpus, dataset and router hashes
preserve raw outputs, errors, identities and measurement artifacts

claims.air_replaces_selected_capability: AIR-only meets all quality, throughput, RAM and lifecycle-energy thresholds with original weights unloaded.
claims.hybrid_saves_cost: Hybrid remains within one percentage point of baseline quality, has no higher measured peak memory and lower lifecycle-adjusted CPU-package energy per correct answer; this does not prove weight replacement.

limitations: Passing factual retrieval does not establish replacement of general-purpose model weights.
The runner and evaluator do not authenticate reviewer assertions or hardware declarations.
CPU-package energy is not external whole-system wall-power measurement.
The bundled development workload is not acceptance evidence.
